Implement:
```rust
/// RAM'deki kapak önbelleği için giriş tavanı: uzun oturumlarda sınırsız
/// büyümeyi engeller. Eski girişler atılır; disk önbelleği olduğundan tekrar
/// ihtiyaç halinde anında geri yüklenir.
const MAX_IMG_CACHE_ENTRIES: usize = 150;

fn trim_img_cache(map: &mut HashMap<String, (u64, Vec<u8>)>) {
    if map.len() <= MAX_IMG_CACHE_ENTRIES { return; }
    let mut keys: Vec<(u64, String)> = map.iter().map(|(k,(t,_))| (*t, k.clone())).collect();
    keys.sort();
    let excess = map.len() - MAX_IMG_CACHE_ENTRIES;
    for (_, k) in keys.into_iter().take(excess) {
        map.remove(&k);
    }
}
```

```rust
fn parse_desktop_exec(path: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let content = std::fs::read_to_string(path).ok()?;
    for line in content.lines() {
        if let Some(v) = line.strip_prefix("Exec=") {
            return Some(v.trim().to_string());
        }
    }
    None
}
```

**Potential optimization areas to consider:**

```rust
fn aniskip_input_conf(t: &api::AniSkipTimes) -> String {
    let fmt_sec = |sec: f64| -> String { let s = sec as u64; format!("{:02}:{:02}", s/60, s%60) };
    let skip_cmd = match (t.op_start, t.op_end) {
        (Some(st), Some(et)) => format!("s seek {et:.1} absolute; show-text \"⏩ İntro Atlandı (AniSkip: {} → {})\" 3000\n", fmt_sec(st), fmt_sec(et)),
        _ => "s show-text \"⚠️ İntro zamanı bulunamadı (AniSkip)\" 2500\n".to_string(),
    };
    let outro_cmd = match (t.ed_start, t.ed_end) {
        (Some(st), Some(et)) => format!("e seek {et:.1} absolute; show-text \"⏩ Outro Atlandı (AniSkip: {} → {})\" 3000\n", fmt_sec(st), fmt_sec(et)),
        _ => "e show-text \"⚠️ Outro zamanı bulunamadı (AniSkip)\" 2500\n".to_string(),
    };
    format!("{skip_cmd}{outro_cmd}S seek -30; show-text \"⏪ 30s Geri\" 2000\nEnd ignore\n")
}
```

vpn.rs design:

```rust
use std::path::PathBuf;

pub const PROXY_PORT: u16 = 10808;

/// sing-box binary + config adaylarını sırayla dener.
pub fn detect() -> Option<(PathBuf, PathBuf)> {
    let home = std::env::var("HOME").ok()?;
    let bin_candidates = [
        format!("{home}/.local/share/singbox/sing-box"),
        format!("{home}/.local/bin/sing-box"),
        "/usr/bin/sing-box".to_string(),
        "/usr/local/bin/sing-box".to_string(),
    ];
    let cfg_candidates = |bin_dir: Option<PathBuf>| -> Vec<PathBuf> { ... };

    // Config arama: binary'nin yanında config.json; sonra ~/.local/share/singbox/config.json,
    // ~/vpn-config.json, ~/sing-box-config.json
    for bin in bin_candidates {
        let p = PathBuf::from(&bin);
        if !p.is_file() { continue; }
        let dir = p.parent().map(|d| d.to_path_buf());
        let mut cfgs = Vec::new();
        if let Some(d)=&dir { cfgs.push(d.join("config.json")); }
        cfgs.push(PathBuf::from(format!("{home}/.local/share/singbox/config.json")));
        cfgs.push(PathBuf::from(format!("{home}/vpn-config.json")));
        cfgs.push(PathBuf::from(format!("{home}/sing-box-config.json")));
        for c in cfgs { if c.is_file() { return Some((p, c)); } }
    }
    None
}

/// Proxy portu ayakta mı? (tünelden bağımsız: 10808 dinleniyor mu)
pub fn port_alive() -> bool {
    std::net::TcpStream::connect_timeout(
        &std::net::SocketAddr::from(([127,0,0,1], PROXY_PORT)),
        std::time::Duration::from_millis(300),
    ).is_ok()
}

/// Tünel gerçekten dışarı mı çıkıyor? (socks üzerinden gstatic 204)
// Bu ağ testi UI'ı bloklamasın diye sadece "Başlat" sonrası kısa doğrulamada kullanılır.
pub fn tunnel_ok() -> bool { curl --socks5 ... } → process run curl? Better use our own reqwest with proxy? reqwest blocking supports socks only with feature. Use std::process Command curl -x socks5h://127.0.0.1:10808 https://www.gstatic.com/generate_204 -o /dev/null -w %{http_code} timeout 8. Acceptable dependency (curl exists on linux desktops typically). Or skip tunnel check; port alive is enough + user sees. Keep tunnel_ok using curl, tolerate absence.

pub fn start(bin:&Path,cfg:&Path)->Result<(),String> {
    // zaten çalışıyor?
    if port_alive() { return Ok(()); }
    let log = log_path();
    let logf = std::fs::OpenOptions::new().create(true).append(true).open(&log).map_err(...)?;
    let errf = logf.try_clone()...;
    std::process::Command::new(bin)
        .arg("run").arg("-c").arg(cfg)
        .stdout(logf).stderr(errf)
        .stdin(Stdio::null())
        .process_group(0)          // std unix ext: ayrık süreç (HUP'tan korunur)
        .spawn().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    // port için bekle
    for _ in 0..20 { if port_alive() { return Ok(());} sleep 250ms }
    Err("süreç başladı ama 10808 portu açılmadı (config hatalı olabilir); log: ...".into())
}

pub fn stop() -> bool {
    // pgrep -f "sing-box run -c" → pid listesi → kill TERM
    let out=Command::new("pgrep").args(["-f","sing-box run"]).output();
    kill each pid via Command kill
}

pub fn log_path() -> PathBuf { ~/.local/share/animecix/singbox.log }

pub fn setup_instructions() -> String { Turkish multi-line }
```

First, vpn.rs stop() improvement. Let me rewrite stop():

```
/// Çalışan sing-box süreçlerini sonlandırır. En az biri öldürüldüyse true.
pub fn stop() -> bool {
    let ok = std::process::Command::new("pgrep")
        .arg("-f")
        .arg("sing-box run")
        .output()
        .ok()
        .map(|o| o.stdout)
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let mut pids = Vec::new();
    for line in String::from_utf8_lossy(&ok).lines() {
        if let Ok(pid) = line.trim().parse::<i32>() {
            pids.push(pid);
        }
    }
    if pids.is_empty() {
        return false;
    }
    for pid in &pids {
        let _ = std::process::Command::new("kill").arg("-TERM").arg(pid.to_string()).status();
    }
    // Portun gerçekten kapanmasını bekle (yumuşak kapanış)
    for _ in 0..16 {
        if !port_alive() {
            return true;
        }
        std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(125));
    }
    // Hâlâ yaşıyorsa sert sonlandır
    for pid in &pids {
        let _ = std::process::Command::new("kill").arg("-KILL").arg(pid.to_string()).status();
    }
    for _ in 0..16 {
        if !port_alive() {
            return true;
        }
        std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(125));
    }
    true
}
```

From the official Flathub docs:
- No definite time limit; reviewers are volunteers.
- Merges done in batches, so waiting varies.

Key accelerators:
- Build and test locally first (flatpak-builder + flatpak-builder-lint) — clean submissions pass faster.
- Complete metainfo (screenshots, content rating), no template removal, minimal AI-generated content in PR description.
- Respond quickly to reviewer comments; comment `bot, build` to start test build.

Also note: after initial approval, updates NEVER go through review again — auto-built. So one-time pain.

Timeline estimate for us:
- Faz 0+1 (our side): a day-ish of work + 20-40min builds.
- Submission → approval: typically a few days to 1-3 weeks (volunteer reviewers). If submission is clean and lints pass, usually within ~a week or two. No guarantee.

```rust
fn timestamp_now() -> String {
    let secs = std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map(|d| d.as_secs())
        .unwrap_or(0);
    let days = secs / 86_400;
    let rem = secs % 86_400;
    let (h, mi, s) = (rem / 3600, (rem % 3600) / 60, rem % 60);
    let (y, m, d) = civil_from_days(days as i64);
    format!("{y:04}-{m:02}-{d:02} {h:02}:{mi:02}:{s:02}")
}

fn civil_from_days(z: i64) -> (i64, u32, u32) {
    // Howard Hinnant algoritması
    let z = z + 719_468;
    let era = if z >= 0 { z } else { z - 146_096 } / 146_097;
    let doe = (z - era * 146_097) as u64;
    let yoe = (doe - doe/1460 + doe/36524 - doe/146096) / 365;
    let y = yoe as i64 + era * 400;
    let doy = doe - (365*yoe + yoe/4 - yoe/100);
    let mp = (5*doy + 2)/153;
    let d = (doy - (153*mp+2)/5 + 1) as u32;
    let m = if mp < 10 { mp + 3 } else { mp - 9 } as u32;
    (if m <= 2 { y + 1 } else { y }, m, d)
}
```

```rust
fn running_in_flatpak() -> bool {
    std::path::Path::new("/.flatpak-info").exists()
}

    if running_in_flatpak() {
        let mut c = std::process::Command::new("flatpak-spawn");

}
```

Hmm cleaner:

```rust
pub fn start(bin: &PathBuf, cfg: &PathBuf) -> Result<(), String> {
    if port_alive() { return Ok(()); }
    use std::io::Write;
    use std::os::unix::process::CommandExt;
    let log = log_path();
    let mut logf = ...;
    let errf = ...;
    let _ = writeln!(logf, "\n[{}] başlatılıyor: {} -c {}", chrono_stamp(), bin.display(), cfg.display());
    let mut cmd;
    if in_flatpak() {
        let home = std::env::var("HOME").unwrap_or_default();
        let mut c = std::process::Command::new("flatpak-spawn");
        c.arg("--host")
         .arg(format!("--env=HOME={home}"))
         .arg(bin);
        cmd = c;
    } else {
        cmd = std::process::Command::new(bin);
    }
    cmd.arg("run").arg("-c").arg(cfg)
       .stdin(null).stdout(logf).stderr(errf)
       .process_group(0).spawn()...
}
```
Wait — flatpak-spawn --host runs the command as a direct child of flatpak-spawn on host; stdout/stderr fds inherited ✓. process_group(0) sets pgid of flatpak-spawn itself; the host-side child may be in different session but TERM/KILL by pid still works since we target sing-box's own pid found via /proc ✓.

YES THAT'S THE BUG: In flatpak manifests, `- cargo-sources.json` as a bare string means "INCLUDE this manifest file's sources" (nested include). But when we replaced it with `type: file ... dest-filename: cargo-sources.json`, we merely download the json INTO the tree — flatpak-builder does NOT recursively load it! The project
NOMM is a stupid simple, super clean "native" (as in it runs on Linux without having to use translation tools...) mod manager for Linux. The goal here is to keep the setup really simple for idiots like me who don't need complex features and all that jazz. Just a few clicks, a clean, modern interface, and you're done :)

Don't come here expecting it to manage mods for something like Skyrim. There are specific tools for that (see NaK or Jackify).

Instead, think of NOMM as more of a general purpose tool for most games that just need you to point to a directory and extract some zip files.

Warning

Gemini had a supporting role in this project, mainly as a learning tool on the UI development side.

For the full AI disclaimer head to the dedicated page on our website.

Our Guiding Principles
No Ads
No Telemetry
No User Account Requirement
Clean & Modern UI/UX
Beginner-friendly
Fully open
How can you add support for a game?
One of the main ideas behind this project is that games are defined by easy to create config .yaml files. This means that anyone can create a simple yaml for their game and submit it to the project with little to no coding knowledge and the tool will automate the rest.

You can find out more info on how to add support for your game here.

"Roadmap"
Phase 1 Development Progress:

 Obtain cool images for game tiles from Steam cache folder
 Display results in a super clean library-style window

Installing/Running
The easiest way to run the app is with flatpak!

To do so :

Go to the releases tab.
Expand the Assets box of the latest version
Click on the nomm.flatpak file to download it
Once downloaded, if you have KDE/GNOME you may simply double click the file. This should boot up KDE Discover or Gnome Software.
Once there you should have a button to install the app, click it.
Once installed, you will see a Launch or Run button appear, click it.
And you're done!

For more advanced users (those who prefer the console or may not have a standard distro)

You may install and run the flatpak via command line: 4. flatpak install nomm.flatpak 5. flatpak run flatpak run moe.nomm.Nomm

From now on when you want to launch it you can just look for it in your start menu (by typing "nomm")

Building
Dependencies
The app is built with:

Python (3.14) -> ...Python...
GTK (>4.0) -> UI framework
Libadwaita -> UI framework
Requests -> requests to nexusmods, gog, epic, etc.
Unrar -> extraction of mods in rar format
vdf -> read steam config files
PyYAML -> read and write yaml files
Prerequisites
To build a flatpak you need to have a distro with flatpak support (most of them do) -> this should normally include the flatpak-builder utility.

Building the app
Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/Allexio/nomm.git
Flatpak
Make the build.sh file executable. From the downloaded folder use this command:
chmod +x ./build/build-flatpak.sh
Run ./build.sh flatpak
Wait for flatpak to be built
You should now have a nomm.flatpak file in the directory
To install your newly obtained flatpak, follow the steps in the "Installing/Running" section above
AUR
Make the build-aur.sh file executable. from the downloaded folder use this command:
chmod +x ./build/build-aur.sh
Run ./build.sh aur
Wait for AUR package to be installed

Kral bu **oyun mod yöneticisi** — Linux'ta oyunlara "mod" (kullanıcı yapımı eklenti/ içerik paketi) kurmayı kolaylaştıran araç:

**Ne yapıyor sırayla:**
1. **Oyunlarını otomatik bulur:** Steam kütüphaneleri, Heroic (Epic/GOG) ve Switch emülatörlerini tarar
2. **Mod indirme linklerini tanır:** Nexus Mods veya GameBanana'dan indirdiğin zip'i ona veriyorsun

5. **Oyunu içinden başlatabilirsin**

**Örnek akış:** Cyberpunk'a grafik modu kuracaksın → Nexus'tan zip indir → NOMM'e sürükle → "Enable" de → oyun. Zip'i elle açıp dosya kopyalamakla uğraşmıyorsun.

**Zekice yanı:** Her oyun için destek, karmaşık kod değil **basit YAML config dosyası** ile tanımlanıyor — yani topluluk kod yazmadan yeni oyun desteği ekleyebiliyor ("SKSE gerekli" gibi özel araçlar bile config'e yazılabiliyor).

```rust
pub(crate) struct Http { inner: Arc<HttpInner> }
```

```rust
fn exec(&self, req: ReqSpec) -> Result<Resp,String> {
    let (tx,rx) = std::sync::mpsc::channel();
    let cl = self.inner.clone();
    self.inner.tx.send(Box::new(move || {
        let _ = tx.send(exec_on(&cl.client, req));
    })).map_err(|_| "arka plan çalıştırıcısı kapandı")?;
    rx.recv().map_err(|_| "arka plan çalıştırıcısı kapandı")?
}
```

Build client on caller thread, move into thread with rt:

```rust
pub fn new(proxy: Option<&str>) -> Result<Self,String> {
    let mut b = wreq::Client::builder()
        .emulation(wreq_util::Emulation::Chrome149)
        .timeout(Duration::from_secs(15))
        .connect_timeout(Duration::from_secs(5));
    if let Some(p) = proxy {
        let pr = wreq::Proxy::all(p).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        b = b.proxy(pr);
    }
    let client = b.build().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel::<Job>();
    let inner_client = client.clone();          // wreq::Client cheap clone
    std::thread::Builder::new().name("http".into()).spawn(move || {
        let rt = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread()
            .enable_all().build().expect("tokio rt");
        let _guard = rt.enter();
        for job in rx { job(&inner_client); }   // jobs run futures via rt.block_on internally
    }).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    Ok(Self{ inner: Arc::new(Inner{client, tx}) })
}
```

```rust
}
```

```rust
pub(crate) struct ReqB<'a>{ http:&'a Http, spec:Spec }
impl ReqB<'_>{
  pub fn header(mut self,k:&str,v:&str)->Self{{headers.push((k.into(),v.into()));}self}
  pub fn query(mut self,q:&[(&str,&str)])->Self{spec.query=Some(q.iter().map(|(a,b)|(a.to_string(),b.to_string())).collect());self}
  pub fn json(mut self,v:&serde_json::Value)->Self{spec.json_body=Some(v.clone());self}
  pub fn timeout(mut self,s:u64)->Self{...}
  pub fn send(self)->Result<Resp,String>{self.http.exec(self.spec)}
  pub fn json<T:DeserializeOwned>(self)->Result<T,String>{self.send()?.error_for_status()?.json()}
}
```

**How to restart the app in GTK/Rust?**
- Re-exec current exe: `std::process::Command::new(std::env::current_exe()...).spawn()` then `std::process::exit(0)`. For AppImage, current_exe is the mounted squashfs path inside /tmp/.mount_XXX — re-exec THAT works only while mount alive; after exit it unmounts! Classic AppImage restart problem. Correct approach for AppImage: use `$APPIMAGE` env var (points to the .AppImage file itself) → spawn $APPIMAGE. Fallback to current_exe otherwise.

```rust
pub fn restart_app() {
    let exe = std::env::var("APPIMAGE")
        .map(PathBuf::from)
        .ok()
        .filter(|p| p.is_file())
        .or_else(|| std::env::current_exe().ok());
    if let Some(exe) = exe {
        let _ = std::process::Command::new(exe).spawn();
        std::process::exit(0);
    }
}
```

Implementation plan (build mode):
In `Http::new`, instead of choosing one transport, build TWO clients: `direct` (no proxy) and `tunnel` (socks5h if port alive). Wrapper tries direct request; on network-error OR 403/5xx?... careful: legitimate 403 from site shouldn't loop. Strategy:

Simplest robust: per-request cascade:
1. attempt with preferred client (direct if available else tunnel)
2. if Err (transport error like timeout/reset) OR status==403 → attempt with the OTHER client (if exists)
3. return first success (2xx..4xx-except-403? no—return whatever second gives)

But careful: search/home returning 403 legitimately? Site uses 403 only as CF block here. Cascade on {Err, 403} is pragmatic.

Preferred order: direct first (fast, no IP-flag risk when ISP allows), fallback tunnel. When ISP drops direct again (like earlier today), direct attempt costs up to timeout (15s!) before falling back — too slow UX. Mitigate: shorter direct timeout? Or remember last-good transport per process: start with last-known-good (default direct), on success store; on failure switch + store. First-call penalty once.

Also port_alive gate: tunnel client only built if port alive at startup (current behavior). If tunnel started later mid-session, still not attached (restart popup covers that flow ✓).

Implementation in http.rs:
```rust
pub(crate) struct Http {
    inner: Arc<Inner>,
}
struct Inner {
    primary: wreq::Client,          // direct
    fallback: Option<wreq::Client>, // tunnel
    last_good: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU8, // 0=primary,1=fallback
    tx: mpsc::Sender<Job>,
}
```
Job carries spec + which client index? exec_on(client,rt,spec). Jobs: send both clients clone + atomic index; job reads index picks client, runs, on Err-or-403 & fallback exists & not already tried → run other; write back used index. Return RawResp.
